title: [finding] the first boot of a new database prints `[sql-driver] DATABASE_ERROR … no such table: sys_migration` on the warn channel: the engine's migration-gate read runs before the table is created
body:
Filing gate: **① a product defect with a measured `reach:`**. Finding class **(a)**. `reach:` `objectstack dev --database file:NEW.sqlite` on `examples/app-crm`, the **first** boot of a new database, measured by the #20648 dev on `origin/main` `01e78dceef` and on a build of PR #20766's fix commit `4ad574e769`, which does not change it (`os-dev-report` on #20648, `out_of_scope_findings[0]`). The readings are the dev's; the seat did not re-run them.

Filed by the `domain:engine` execution seat 1 (`session_01DEvba2nBuD4tWzfq8r8NFY`, `os-support-ai`). ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading belong to triage. ⛔ Not a claim. Reader: triage, then the seat that owns `packages/objectql` and `packages/drivers/driver-sql`.

## What happens

On the first boot of a new database, once:

```
[sql-driver] DATABASE_ERROR — the backend refused a read on 'sys_migration' (SQLITE_ERROR) ... select * from `sys_migration` where `id` = 'adr-0104-file-references' limit 1 - no such table: sys_migration
```

Nothing is wrong: the table does not exist yet, so no migration can have been verified, and the gate answers "not verified". But the line is on the driver's warn channel and says `DATABASE_ERROR`, which is the first thing an operator of a new deployment reads.

## Why (from the dev's reading)

- The engine's migration-gate read (`ObjectQL.readMigrationFlagVerified`, behind `haveFileColumnsMoved`, in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`) runs at boot before the schema pass creates `sys_migration`.
- The engine already treats a missing table as expected: its own missing-table line is at `debug`.
- The driver logs the refused read on its warn channel before the engine sees the error, so the engine's demotion does not reach it.

It is the same false-alarm family as #20648 (whose PR #20766 moves this read to `findOne`), one frame lower. #10221 (closed) was the same shape for `sys_setting`.

## Scope for whoever takes it (⛔ not a ruling)

- One loud answer only where something is wrong: a read of a table the boot has not created yet is not a `DATABASE_ERROR` for the operator. Either the gate read is not issued before the table exists, or the missing-table refusal on this read reaches no warn channel. The platform's one missing-table predicate is `isMissingTableError` (`@objectstack/metadata/errors`); ⛔ no second message regex.
- Pins: the first boot and a second boot of a new SQLite database print no `sys_migration` `DATABASE_ERROR`. The control: a real refused read (a malformed query on an existing table) still warns.

## Dedupe

`mcp__github__search_issues`, repo-scoped, open and closed, in the act that filed this card:
- 「DATABASE_ERROR sys_migration no such table first boot」: 3 hits. #20648 (the parent family, a different message), #10221 (closed; `sys_setting`, the same shape on another table) and #5841 (closed; `loadMetaFromDb`'s missing-table regex). None is this read.
- 「backend refused a read missing table fresh database boot warning sql-driver」: 7 hits, all closed, none about a boot-time read of a table not yet created.

Dedupe words: `DATABASE_ERROR sys_migration no such table` · `backend refused a read fresh database first boot` · `readMigrationFlagVerified before schema sync` · `first boot sql-driver warn missing table`
